sentences.text:
. By the present appeal, the appellant challenges the judgment dated 18.12.2024 (hereafter 'impugned judgment') and order on sentence dated 01.08.2025 (hereafter 'impugned order on sentence'), passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge ('ASJ') in SC No. 12/2014 arising out of FIR No. 200/2012, registered at Police Station Safdarjung Enclave.
2.
By the impugned judgment, the appellant was convicted for the offences under Sections 498A/306/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 ('IPC').
3. By the impugned order on sentence, the appellant was sentenced to undergo simple imprisonment for a period of two years for offence under Section 306 of the IPC.
The appellant was directed to undergo simple imprisonment for a period of one This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 09/08/2025 at 00:25:19 year for offence under Section 498A of the IPC.
The appellant was also directed to pay a fine of 15,000/- to the LRs of deceased, and in case of default of payment of fine, to undergo simple imprisonment for a period of two months.
Both the sentences were directed to run concurrently.

4. The impugned order on sentence was suspended by the learned ASJ and the appellant was admitted to bail for a period of 30 days on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of 20,000/- with one surety of the like amount and during the said period, the sentence was directed to be deemed to be suspended, in order to enable the appellant to file an appeal before this Court.
5.
The matter requires consideration.

sentences.text: The appeal is admitted.

7. Let the Trial Court Record be requisitioned.
8.
List in due course.
The present application is filed seeking suspension of sentence of the appellant during the pendency of the present appeal.
10. The learned counsel for the appellant / applicant submits that the appellant was the father-in-law of the victim and he had nothing to do with the victim.
He submits that he has been erroneously convicted in the present case.
11. He submits that the appellant has already spent four months in custody during the course of the trial and after being released on bail, has never misused his liberty.
12. The appellant is a senior citizen and there are no chances of him absconding.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 09/08/2025 at 00:25:19 13.
Considering the Board position of this Court, the final hearing of the present appeal is not likely to take place in near future.

14. In view of the above, the impugned order on sentence is suspended till the pendency of the present appeal, on the strength of the personal bond and surety furnished by the appellant before the learned ASJ, on the following conditions:
a.
The appellant shall deposit the fine amount as imposed by the impugned order on sentence within a period of four weeks of his release.
Proof of deposit of fine to be furnished to the concerned IO/SHO;
b. The appellant shall under no circumstance leave the country without the permission of this Court;
c. The appellant shall give his mobile number to the concerned IO/SHO and shall keep his mobile phone switched on at all times;

d. The appellant shall provide the address where he is residing and shall not change the address without informing the concerned IO/ SHO;
e.
The appellant shall appear before this Court as and when directed.
